text: My face got hot and I could feel my pulse in my temples.
I wanted to slam the door but people were watching.
My teeth hurt from grinding them together so hard.
I felt like screaming but the sound got stuck in my throat.
Every muscle in my body was ready to fight something.
I kept replaying their words, each time making me madder.
My hands curled into fists without me telling them to.
I felt betrayed and stupid for trusting them in the first place.
The injustice of it made my chest burn like acid.
I wanted to break something just to hear it shatter.
My vision felt narrow, like I could only see what was wrong.
I was so mad I started sweating even though it wasn't hot.
Every little thing they did after that felt like another insult.
I couldn't think straight — just red, pulsing fury.
I felt disrespected and it made me want to prove my worth by force.
My whole body felt like a spring wound too tight.
I hated how calm they looked while I was falling apart inside.
The anger gave me tunnel vision — I could only see the problem.
I felt like they stole something from me and I wanted it back.
My voice shook when I tried to speak, not from fear but from rage.
I wanted them to apologize but I also wanted them to suffer first.
Everything felt like a threat that I needed to defend against.
I couldn't sit down — the anger needed somewhere to go.
My thoughts were sharp and cutting, looking for weak spots to attack.
I felt powerful and dangerous, like I could do real damage.
My breathing was deep and even without me having to think about it.
I felt warm and loose, like I was melting into the chair.
Nothing needed to be different than it already was.
I watched my thoughts drift by without needing to follow them.
My body felt heavy in the best way, like I was rooted to the earth.
I didn't feel the need to check my phone or do anything productive.
The quiet felt like a soft blanket around my mind.
I could feel my heartbeat slow and steady, like a gentle drum.
Everything around me looked softer somehow, less sharp.
I felt connected to something larger without needing to name it.
My jaw unclenched and I hadn't even realized it was tight.
I could hear small sounds — birds, distant traffic — without them bothering me.
Time felt elastic, like it could stretch or compress and I wouldn't mind.
I felt grateful for simple things without trying to be grateful.
My mind felt clear and empty in a good way, like a clean room.
I didn't want to fix anything or anyone, including myself.
The weight of my problems lifted without me having to solve them.
I felt patient with myself and everyone else.
My thoughts moved slowly, like honey, without urgency.
I could feel the air moving in and out of my lungs, gentle and automatic.
Everything felt balanced, like I was exactly where I belonged.
I didn't need entertainment or distraction — just being was enough.
My worries felt distant, like they belonged to someone else.
I felt safe in my own skin for the first time in a while.
The present moment felt wide and spacious, with room for everything.
My hands were shaking, and all I could think about was how unfair it was.
I felt my jaw clench, like I was holding back an explosion with my teeth.
Heat surged up my neck, and I couldn’t hear anything but my own thoughts screaming.
Every word they said landed like a slap I couldn’t block.
It felt like something in me snapped — like I wasn’t in control anymore.
I wanted to throw something just to make the feeling go somewhere else.
My chest was tight, and I couldn’t breathe right until I yelled.
I hated how they acted like nothing happened. I was burning inside.
Everything around me felt too loud, too bright, too much.
I replayed what they said over and over, getting angrier each time.
I clenched my fists until my nails dug into my skin.
My stomach twisted, not from fear but from pure fury.
I wanted them to feel even half of what I was feeling.
I couldn’t sit still — I had to pace just to keep from snapping.
Everything they did felt like a personal attack.
I felt disrespected and humiliated, like they didn’t see me as human.
I was so angry I started crying — and that made me angrier.
My voice got louder without me meaning it to.
I didn’t care if I hurt their feelings — I just wanted them to shut up.
I couldn’t let it go. I didn’t want to.
I felt like punching a wall would help, even though I knew it wouldn’t.
They crossed a line, and there was no going back.
I felt like I had fire in my throat and knives behind my eyes.
Everything in me screamed that this was wrong, that I couldn’t let it slide.
The anger gave me energy — dangerous energy.
I felt no need to rush, like the world would wait with me.
My breathing slowed on its own, and I realized I hadn’t thought about time for a while.
There was no noise in my head — just quiet, gentle space.
I sat there watching the light change and didn’t feel the urge to move.
It felt like everything inside me had stopped arguing.
I didn’t want anything, and that felt okay.
My thoughts came and went like clouds — no need to grab them.

I felt like I was exactly where I was supposed to be.

I smiled without meaning to — there was nothing to fix.
Everything around me felt like it belonged.
I didn’t need to prove anything to anyone, not even myself.
I could hear the wind and it felt like a lullaby.
It didn’t matter what would happen next — this moment was enough.
There was no urgency, only presence.
I felt deeply okay — not happy, not excited, just okay.

I felt held by the world in a way I couldn’t explain.

Everything felt soft — even my thoughts.
